name: POET Technologies Inc.
title: POET Technologies — the optical interposer pre-revenue bet on co-packaged optics
subtitle: A $313M cash war chest, no commercial revenue, and an architecture pitch that requires hyperscalers to abandon pluggable transceivers — how POET's photonic-integration story trades pure option value
abstract: POET Technologies Inc. (POET, dual-listed on NASDAQ and the TSX) is a pre-commercial photonics company that designs and licenses the POET Optical Interposer — a wafer-level photonic integration platform positioned to enable co-packaged optics (CPO) and external light source (ELS) modules at 800G, 1.6T and beyond for AI data center interconnect. The company is led by Dr. Suresh Venkatesan, who joined as Chairman and CEO in 2015 from his prior role as SVP of Technology Development at GlobalFoundries (where he led the 28nm ramp and 14nm transfer) and earlier as a Freescale Fellow / Motorola SABA inductee. FY2025 produced essentially no commercial revenue — non-recurring engineering and product receipts of approximately $1.2 million for the full year (Q3 2025 $298K, Q4 2025 $341K) against a net loss of $62.96 million and R&D spend of $18.08 million. The story is not revenue, it is balance sheet: total assets grew from $69.7 million (Dec 2024) to $328.6 million (Dec 2025), and cash plus short-term investments stand at $313.4 million — the product of a $250 million institutional equity financing closed in 2025 from three undisclosed institutional buyers. Share count is 132.3 million common shares with 5.79 million options and 37.36 million warrants outstanding, representing potential dilution of 28.35%. A $135.6 million derivative warrant liability sits on the balance sheet against working capital of $170.7 million. The board pairs Venkatesan with Lead Independent Director Jean-Louis Malinge (ex-CEO of silicon-photonics pioneer Kotura, sold to Mellanox 2013), Glen Riley (32-year semiconductor/optoelectronics operator, ex-Qorvo / TriQuint / Agere / Lucent), Theresa Lan Ende (Arista Networks CPO, ex-Cisco supply chain), Robert Tirva (ex-Sonim CFO/COO, IBM/Broadcom/Dropbox), and Sohail Khan (newly appointed July 2025, ex-Coherent/SiC EVP, ex-Agere CEO, ex-ViXS CEO). Chris Tsiofas retired after 13 years as Audit Committee Chair at the June 2025 AGM. POET's investment proposition is binary: if hyperscalers adopt CPO at scale and POET's optical interposer becomes a qualified component in the supply chain, the platform thesis is durable; if pluggable optics continue to dominate or competing interposer architectures win, the $313M cash is a multi-year runway against a thesis that may not crystallise inside it.
